answer_text:
# 🤰 How to Read Pregnancy Test Results

Here is a comprehensive guide to understanding pregnancy test results:

---

## 🔬 How the Test Works

Home pregnancy tests are designed to identify the presence of a specific hormone in your urine: human chorionic gonadotropin, commonly known as hCG. hCG levels are initially very low but double approximately every 48 to 72 hours in early pregnancy.

---

## ✅ Positive Result (PREGNANT)

A pregnancy test is **positive** when **two lines** appear – one in the Control (C) region and one in the Test (T) region. Even if the second line is faint, it still indicates the presence of hCG hormone, confirming pregnancy.

- **Digital tests** are the easiest to read. The result window will clearly say **"Pregnant"** or **"Yes"** if you're pregnant.
- **Single-window tests** will show **two lines** side-by-side if the test is positive. One line is the control line, and the second line is the result line.
- **Two-window tests** will show a line in the smaller control window and a **plus "+" sign** in the larger, second window.

---

## ❌ Negative Result (NOT PREGNANT)

A **negative result** shows **only one color band** on the top Control (C) region. There should be no apparent band on the Test (T) region.

- A digital test will say **"Not Pregnant"** or **"No"** if you're not pregnant.

---

## ⚠️ Invalid Result

If **no line appears**, or there's only one line in the (T) and not in the (C), the test is **invalid**. A blurry or unreadable test window also indicates invalid results. If there is no visible control line, discard the test and repeat with a new device.

---

## 🔍 Faint Lines – What Do They Mean?

A very common sight is a faint, almost ghostly test line. In the vast majority of cases, **a faint line is a positive line**. It indicates that hCG is present, but the concentration in your urine may still be relatively low. This is typical in very early pregnancy.

---

## 💧 Evaporation Lines – Don't Be Fooled

An **evaporation line** (or "evap line") is a faint, colorless streak that can appear in the test window **after** the urine has dried and the designated reading time has passed. It is **not** a positive result — it is a residue left by the evaporated urine.

Distinguishing faint lines from evaporation lines comes down to **timing and color**. A faint (positive) line will appear within the recommended window of time (usually within 3–5 minutes) and will activate the dye in the test, so it can appear blue or light pink in color.

---

## ⏰ When to Read the Test

You'll want to read your test **between 5 and 10 minutes** after taking it. Beyond that window, you may see an evaporation line, which isn't the same as a positive.

---

## 🕐 Best Time to Take the Test

For the most accurate result, use your **first-morning urine**. This sample is typically more concentrated and contains the highest level of hCG if you are pregnant. As the day progresses and you drink fluids, your urine becomes more diluted, which can make a very early low level of hCG more difficult to detect.

---

## ❗ False Results

| Type | Meaning | Common Causes |
|------|---------|--------------|
| **False Negative** | Test says NOT pregnant, but you ARE | Testing too early, diluted urine, expired test, incorrect use |
| **False Positive** | Test says PREGNANT, but you're NOT | Fertility medications with hCG, recent miscarriage, certain medical conditions |

False-negative results are **more common** than false-positive results. If your pregnancy test is negative, but you still don't get your period in two days, take another test.

---

## 👩‍⚕️ Next Steps

A home pregnancy test is a **screening tool** and should not be used as the only basis for diagnosis. Your healthcare provider should confirm pregnancy based on a full clinical evaluation.

> **Always consult a doctor to confirm your results, especially before making any medical decisions.**
